received_content.title: RT-to-GR Bridge Through One-DOF Projection, Bounded Symmetry, and Failure of Distinguishable Extension

executive_claim.statement: A realized extreme-curvature RT evaluates many admissible relational orientations into one degree of freedom. Projection of that one-degree-of-freedom result does not produce an ontological zero-state. It produces bounded symmetry: one existing condition within which all admissible candidates are indistinguishable. Because extension requires a distinguishable successor, bounded symmetry admits no distinct continuation. GR represents the absence of a valid causal-geometric continuation as geodesic incompleteness.
executive_claim.compact_form: many -> one DOF -> bounded symmetry -> no distinguishable successor -> GR geodesic incompleteness
executive_claim.core_correction: The bridge does not preserve one RT degree of freedom as one GR rank, and it does not project one degree of freedom into ontological zero. It projects one degree of freedom into one bounded symmetry condition whose set of distinguishable extensions is empty.
